THE STORY OF YOSEF — CHAPTERS 38 THROUGH 45

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 38 Yehudah and Tamar

38:1 And it came to pass at that time, that Yehudah went down from his brothers, and turned in to a certain Adulami man, whose name was Chirah.

38:2 And Yehudah saw there a daughter of a certain Kena'ani man, whose name was Shua; and he took her, and went in to her.

38:3 And she conceived, and bore a son; and he called his name Er.

38:4 And she conceived again, and bore a son; and she called his name Onan.

38:5 And she yet again bore a son, and called his name Shelah; and he was at Kheziv, when she bore him.

38:6 And Yehudah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

38:7 And Er, Yehudah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of YHWH; and YHWH put him to death.

38:8 And Yehudah said to Onan: Go in to your brother's wife, and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.

38:9 And Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in to his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give offspring to his brother.

38:10 And the thing which he did was wicked in the sight of YHWH; and he put him to death also.

38:11 Then Yehudah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law: Remain a widow in your father's house, until Shelah my son grows up — for he feared, lest he also die, like his brothers. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.

38:12 And in process of time the daughter of Shua, Yehudah's wife, died; and Yehudah was comforted, and went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Chirah the Adulami.

38:13 And it was told to Tamar, saying: Behold, your father-in-law goes up to Timnah to shear his sheep.

38:14 And she put off her widow's garments from her, and covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat at the entrance of Einayim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she was not given to him as wife.

38:15 When Yehudah saw her, he thought her to be a prostitute; for she had covered her face.

38:16 And he turned to her by the way, and said: Come, please, let me come in to you — for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said: What will you give me, that you may come in to me?

38:17 And he said: I will send you a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said: Will you give me a pledge, until you send it?

38:18 And he said: What pledge shall I give you? And she said: Your signet, and your cords, and your staff that is in your hand. And he gave them to her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him.

38:19 And she arose, and went away, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

38:20 And Yehudah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adulami, to receive the pledge from the woman's hand; but he did not find her.

38:21 Then he asked the men of her place, saying: Where is the prostitute, who was at Einayim by the wayside? And they said: There has been no prostitute here.

38:22 And he returned to Yehudah, and said: I have not found her; and also the men of the place said, There has been no prostitute here.

38:23 And Yehudah said: Let her take it for herself, lest we be shamed; behold, I sent this kid, and you have not found her.

38:24 And it came to pass about three months later, that it was told Yehudah, saying: Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot; and moreover, behold, she is with child by harlotry. And Yehudah said: Bring her out, and let her be burned.

38:25 When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying: By the man whose these are, am I with child; and she said: Discern, please, whose are these — the signet, and the cords, and the staff.

38:26 And Yehudah acknowledged them, and said: She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

38:27 And it came to pass at the time of her travail, that behold, twins were in her womb.

38:28 And it came to pass, when she travailed, that one put out a hand; and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying: This came out first.

38:29 And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that behold, his brother came out; and she said: What a breach you have made for yourself! Therefore his name was called Peretz.

38:30 And afterward came out his brother, who had the scarlet thread upon his hand; and his name was called Zerach.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 26's צדקה ממני ("she is more righteous than I") is rendered literally; the phrase carries a real, disclosed dual sense noted in scholarship -- a legal/forensic "more in the right" and a moral "more righteous" -- both plausible from the Hebrew, neither forced to the exclusion of the other. Verse 29's פרץ (Peretz, "breach") receives its own explicit in-text etymology, consistent with the book's recurring naming pattern; rendered as a disclosed transliteration rather than translated into the verse. This chapter interrupts the Yosef narrative already begun at ch.37 and resumed at ch.39 -- a real, long-noted structural feature of the received text, presented here exactly as MT places it, without relocating or commenting on the insertion beyond this note.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 39 Yosef and Potifar's Wife

39:1 And Yosef was brought down to Mitzrayim; and Potifar, an officer of Par'oh's, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Yishme'elim, who had brought him down there.

39:2 And YHWH was with Yosef, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

39:3 And his master saw that YHWH was with him, and that YHWH made all that he did to prosper in his hand.

39:4 And Yosef found favor in his sight, and he served him; and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

39:5 And it came to pass from the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that YHWH blessed the Egyptian's house for Yosef's sake; and the blessing of YHWH was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.

39:6 And he left all that he had in Yosef's hand; and he knew not anything he had, except the bread which he ate. And Yosef was of beautiful form, and fair to look upon.

39:7 And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Yosef; and she said: Lie with me.

39:8 But he refused, and said to his master's wife: Behold, my master does not know what is with me in the house, and he has put all that he has into my hand.

39:9 There is no one greater in this house than I; nor has he kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife; how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against the Creator?

39:10 And it came to pass, as she spoke to Yosef day by day, that he did not listen to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.

39:11 And it came to pass on a certain day, when he went into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the house was there inside,

39:12 that she caught him by his garment, saying: Lie with me; and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got outside.

39:13 And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and had fled outside,

39:14 that she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying: See, he has brought in a Hebrew to us to mock us; he came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.

39:15 And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled, and got outside.

39:16 And she laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.

39:17 And she spoke to him according to these words, saying: The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me;

39:18 and it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled outside.

39:19 And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, After this manner did your servant to me — that his wrath was kindled.

39:20 And Yosef's master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound; and he was there in the prison.

39:21 But YHWH was with Yosef, and showed him kindness, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

39:22 And the keeper of the prison committed to Yosef's hand all the prisoners who were in the prison; and whatever they did there, he was the doer of it.

39:23 The keeper of the prison did not look after anything that was under his hand, because YHWH was with him; and that which he did, YHWH made it prosper.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] This chapter is unusual within the Yosef narrative for its dense concentration of יהוה (six occurrences: vv.2, 3 [x2], 5 [x2], 21, 23 [x2]) in a section otherwise dominated by אלהים and by no divine name at all across long stretches -- disclosed as a real distributional observation, not assigned a source-critical explanation. Verse 9's ואיך אעשה הרעה הגדלה הזאת וחטאתי לאלהים ("how can I do this great wickedness, and sin against the Creator") is Yosef's own words, spoken in a foreign court to a foreign household -- rendered per standing policy without assuming his phrase means something different than it would in a fully Israelite context, since the text itself does not qualify or distinguish it.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 40 Yosef Interprets the Cupbearer and Baker's Dreams

40:1 And it came to pass after these things, that the cupbearer of the king of Mitzrayim and his baker offended their lord the king of Mitzrayim.

40:2 And Par'oh was angry against his two officers, against the chief of the cupbearers, and against the chief of the bakers.

40:3 And he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Yosef was bound.

40:4 And the captain of the guard charged Yosef with them, and he served them; and they continued a season in custody.

40:5 And they dreamed a dream, both of them, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Mitzrayim, who were bound in the prison.

40:6 And Yosef came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and behold, they were sad.

40:7 And he asked Par'oh's officers who were with him in custody in his master's house, saying: Why do you look so sad today?

40:8 And they said to him: We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. And Yosef said to them: Do not interpretations belong to the Creator? Tell it to me, please.

40:9 And the chief cupbearer told his dream to Yosef, and said to him: In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;

40:10 and in the vine were three branches; and it was as though it budded, and its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes.

40:11 And Par'oh's cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Par'oh's cup, and gave the cup into Par'oh's hand.

40:12 And Yosef said to him: This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days.

40:13 Within yet three days shall Par'oh lift up your head, and restore you to your office; and you shall give Par'oh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when you were his cupbearer.

40:14 But have me in your remembrance when it shall be well with you, and show kindness, please, to me, and make mention of me to Par'oh, and bring me out of this house.

40:15 For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews; and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.

40:16 When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Yosef: I also saw in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head;

40:17 and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of baked food for Par'oh; and the birds ate them out of the basket upon my head.

40:18 And Yosef answered and said: This is the interpretation of it: the three baskets are three days.

40:19 Within yet three days shall Par'oh lift up your head from off you, and shall hang you on a tree; and the birds shall eat your flesh from off you.

40:20 And it came to pass on the third day, which was Par'oh's birthday, that he made a feast to all his servants; and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and of the chief baker among his servants.

40:21 And he restored the chief cupbearer to his cupbearing again; and he gave the cup into Par'oh's hand.

40:22 But he hanged the chief baker, as Yosef had interpreted to them.

40:23 Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Yosef, but forgot him.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 8's הלוא לאלהים פתרנים ("do not interpretations belong to the Creator") introduces the interpretive framework that governs the remainder of the Yosef narrative -- that dream-interpretation is not Yosef's own skill but the Creator's revelation through him; rendered literally without added theological commentary. Verse 13's ("lift up your head") and v.19's identical phrase applied to the baker's execution are a real, deliberate wordplay preserved in translation: the same Hebrew idiom (נשא ראש) is used for both restoration and death, with the different outcome carried entirely by the following clause rather than the idiom itself -- both renderings kept parallel rather than varied to avoid the ambiguity.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 41 Par'oh's Dreams — Yosef Rules Egypt

41:1 And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Par'oh dreamed; and behold, he stood by the river.

41:2 And behold, there came up out of the river seven cows, well favored and fat-fleshed; and they fed in the reed grass.

41:3 And behold, seven other cows came up after them out of the river, ill favored and lean-fleshed; and stood by the other cows upon the bank of the river.

41:4 And the ill favored and lean-fleshed cows ate up the seven well favored and fat cows. So Par'oh awoke.

41:5 And he slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, full and good.

41:6 And behold, seven ears, thin and blighted with the east wind, sprang up after them.

41:7 And the thin ears swallowed up the seven full and good ears. And Par'oh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

41:8 And it came to pass in the morning, that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Mitzrayim, and all its wise men; and Par'oh told them his dream, but there was no one who could interpret it to Par'oh.

41:9 Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Par'oh, saying: I remember my faults today.

41:10 Par'oh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker.

41:11 And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream.

41:12 And there was with us there a young Hebrew man, a servant of the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted our dreams to us; to each man he interpreted according to his own dream.

41:13 And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; he restored me to my office, and he hanged the baker.

41:14 Then Par'oh sent and called for Yosef, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon; and he shaved, and changed his garments, and came in to Par'oh.

41:15 And Par'oh said to Yosef: I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it; and I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.

41:16 And Yosef answered Par'oh, saying: It is not in me; the Creator will give Par'oh an answer of peace.

41:17 And Par'oh spoke to Yosef: In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the river;

41:18 and behold, there came up out of the river seven cows, fat-fleshed and well favored; and they fed in the reed grass.

41:19 And behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ill favored and lean-fleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Mitzrayim for ugliness.

41:20 And the lean and ill favored cows ate up the first seven fat cows.

41:21 And when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they were still ill favored, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

41:22 And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears came up upon one stalk, full and good.

41:23 And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blighted with the east wind, sprang up after them.

41:24 And the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears; and I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could declare it to me.

41:25 And Yosef said to Par'oh: The dream of Par'oh is one; what the Creator is about to do he has declared to Par'oh.

41:26 The seven good cows are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream is one.

41:27 And the seven lean and ill favored cows that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty ears blighted with the east wind — they shall be seven years of famine.

41:28 That is the thing which I spoke to Par'oh; what the Creator is about to do he has shown to Par'oh.

41:29 Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Mitzrayim.

41:30 And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Mitzrayim, and the famine shall consume the land;

41:31 and the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows, for it shall be very grievous.

41:32 And for the dream being doubled to Par'oh twice, it is because the thing is established by the Creator, and the Creator will shortly bring it to pass.

41:33 Now therefore let Par'oh look for a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Mitzrayim.

41:34 Let Par'oh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Mitzrayim in the seven years of plenty.

41:35 And let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Par'oh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

41:36 And the food shall be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Mitzrayim, that the land not perish through the famine.

41:37 And the thing was good in the eyes of Par'oh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

41:38 And Par'oh said to his servants: Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the spirit of the gods?

41:39 And Par'oh said to Yosef: Since the Creator has shown you all this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.

41:40 You shall be over my house, and according to your word shall all my people be ruled; only in the throne will I be greater than you.

41:41 And Par'oh said to Yosef: See, I have set you over all the land of Mitzrayim.

41:42 And Par'oh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it upon Yosef's hand, and arrayed him in garments of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

41:43 And he made him ride in his second chariot; and they cried before him: Bow the knee. And he set him over all the land of Mitzrayim.

41:44 And Par'oh said to Yosef: I am Par'oh, and without you no man shall lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Mitzrayim.

41:45 And Par'oh called Yosef's name Tzafenat-Pane'ach; and he gave him Osnat, the daughter of Poti-Fera priest of On, as wife. And Yosef went out over the land of Mitzrayim.

41:46 And Yosef was thirty years old when he stood before Par'oh king of Mitzrayim. And Yosef went out from the presence of Par'oh, and went throughout all the land of Mitzrayim.

41:47 And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth abundantly.

41:48 And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Mitzrayim, and laid up the food in the cities; the food of the field, which was around every city, he laid up in it.

41:49 And Yosef gathered grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting; for it was without number.

41:50 And to Yosef were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Osnat, the daughter of Poti-Fera priest of On, bore to him.

41:51 And Yosef called the name of the firstborn Menasheh; for, he said, the Creator has made me forget all my trouble, and all my father's house.

41:52 And the name of the second he called Efrayim; for the Creator has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.

41:53 And the seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Mitzrayim, came to an end.

41:54 And the seven years of famine began to come, as Yosef had said; and there was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Mitzrayim there was bread.

41:55 And when all the land of Mitzrayim was famished, the people cried to Par'oh for bread; and Par'oh said to all the Egyptians: Go to Yosef; what he says to you, do.

41:56 And the famine was over all the face of the earth; and Yosef opened all the storehouses, and sold to the Egyptians; and the famine grew severe in the land of Mitzrayim.

41:57 And all the earth came to Mitzrayim, to Yosef, to buy grain; because the famine was severe in all the earth.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 38's רוח אלהים ("spirit of the gods/of the Creator") is a real, disclosed ambiguity: Par'oh, a polytheistic Egyptian king, is the speaker, and Hebrew אלהים is grammatically compatible with either a singular or a generic/plural divine referent. Rendered "spirit of the gods" (lowercase), consistent with the standing policy that foreign speakers' generic religious language is not silently converted into a reference to Israel's own deity absent textual signal that they mean YHWH specifically -- disclosed here as a translator decision, not a claim about what Par'oh actually believed. Verse 45's צפנת פענח (Tzafenat-Pane'ach) is a real Egyptian name conferred on Yosef; retained as a transliteration rather than translated, since rendering its disputed Egyptian etymology into English would import a specific scholarly reconstruction not present in the Hebrew text itself. Verses 51-52 continue the naming-etymology pattern (Menasheh from נשה, "to forget"; Efrayim from פרה, "to be fruitful"), both disclosed as the text's own embedded wordplay.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 42 The Brothers Go Down to Mitzrayim

42:1 Now Ya'akov saw that there was grain in Mitzrayim, and Ya'akov said to his sons: Why do you look at one another?

42:2 And he said: Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Mitzrayim; go down there, and buy for us from there, that we may live, and not die.

42:3 And Yosef's ten brothers went down to buy grain in Mitzrayim.

42:4 But Binyamin, Yosef's brother, Ya'akov did not send with his brothers; for he said: Lest harm befall him.

42:5 And the sons of Yisra'el came to buy grain among those who came; for the famine was in the land of Kena'an.

42:6 And Yosef was the governor over the land; he it was who sold to all the people of the land; and Yosef's brothers came, and bowed down to him with their faces to the earth.

42:7 And Yosef saw his brothers, and knew them, but made himself strange to them, and spoke roughly with them; and he said to them: Where do you come from? And they said: From the land of Kena'an, to buy food.

42:8 And Yosef knew his brothers, but they did not know him.

42:9 Then Yosef remembered the dreams which he had dreamed about them, and said to them: You are spies; you have come to see the nakedness of the land.

42:10 And they said to him: No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

42:11 We are all one man's sons; we are honest men; your servants are not spies.

42:12 And he said to them: No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land.

42:13 And they said: Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Kena'an; and behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more.

42:14 And Yosef said to them: That is what I spoke to you, saying, You are spies.

42:15 By this you shall be tested: by the life of Par'oh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.

42:16 Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and you shall be kept in prison, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you; or else, by the life of Par'oh, surely you are spies.

42:17 And he put them all together into custody three days.

42:18 And Yosef said to them on the third day: This do, and live; for I fear the Creator.

42:19 If you are honest men, let one of your brothers be bound in your prison house; but go, carry grain for the famine of your households;

42:20 and bring your youngest brother to me; so shall your words be verified, and you shall not die. And they did so.

42:21 And they said one to another: We are truly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he pleaded with us, and we would not listen; therefore this distress has come upon us.

42:22 And Re'uven answered them, saying: Did I not speak to you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and you would not listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.

42:23 And they did not know that Yosef understood them; for the interpreter was between them.

42:24 And he turned himself away from them, and wept; and he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Shim'on from among them, and bound him before their eyes.

42:25 Then Yosef commanded to fill their vessels with grain, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way; and thus he did to them.

42:26 And they loaded their donkeys with the grain, and departed from there.

42:27 And as one of them opened his sack to give his donkey provender in the lodging place, he saw his money; and behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

42:28 And he said to his brothers: My money is restored; and behold, it is even in my sack; and their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying: What is this that the Creator has done to us?

42:29 And they came to Ya'akov their father, to the land of Kena'an, and told him all that had befallen them, saying:

42:30 The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us, and took us for spies of the land.

42:31 And we said to him: We are honest men; we are no spies.

42:32 We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Kena'an.

42:33 And the man, the lord of the land, said to us: By this I shall know that you are honest men — leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your households, and go your way;

42:34 and bring your youngest brother to me; then shall I know that you are no spies, but that you are honest men; so I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.

42:35 And it came to pass, as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man's bundle of money was in his sack; and when they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.

42:36 And Ya'akov their father said to them: You have bereaved me of my children; Yosef is no more, and Shim'on is no more, and you will take Binyamin away; upon me are all these things come.
